title: Escape to Host
description: An adversary breaks out of a container's isolation boundary to gain access to the underlying host kernel and filesystem. In Kubernetes, the highest-frequency primitives are: a privileged pod (capabilities give the container kernel-level reach), a hostPath mount that exposes the host filesystem (or the docker.sock or kubelet credentials) into the container, sharing the host PID/Network/IPC namespace, or abusing CRI-internal sockets. Detection is anchored on the pod spec (declared intent), the runtime sensor (observed escape syscalls and namespace transitions), and the API audit log (the principal that created the offending pod).

microsoft_k8s_matrix.name: Writable hostPath mount
microsoft_k8s_matrix.description: A container with a writable hostPath mount (or, equivalently, a privileged container with host namespace sharing) can read and modify host filesystem state, container runtime sockets, and kubelet credentials, leading to host-level execution.

data_components.name: Container Creation
data_components.definition: Initial construction of a new container, including security context (privileged, capabilities), namespace settings (hostPID, hostNetwork, hostIPC), and volume mounts. The escape primitives are declared in the spec, so this component carries the highest pre-runtime signal.
relevant_events: Pod manifest with capabilities.add containing SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, or SYS_PTRACE

data_components.name: Process Creation
data_components.definition: Process creation events captured by an in-cluster runtime sensor, with namespace and capability context. Escape attempts surface as processes that transition out of the container's PID/mount namespace, or that exec via the container runtime socket from inside the container.
relevant_events: Process exec where the parent is in container PID namespace and the child is in init namespace (mount or PID namespace transition)
exec of nsenter, unshare, chroot, or runc inside a container
exec of crictl, ctr, kubectl, or docker against the docker.sock or containerd.sock from inside a container

data_components.name: OS API Execution
data_components.definition: Direct kernel API and syscall observation. Container escape via syscalls (unshare, setns, keyctl, mount, pivot_root) is captured at this layer by an eBPF or LSM-based sensor. (Equilibrium previously labeled this DS0028 Logon Session in error; corrected per upstream cross-reference.)
relevant_events: Syscall trace: unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) followed by mount() of host paths from inside a container
Syscall trace: setns() onto a host namespace fd opened from /proc/1/ns
Syscall trace: keyctl manipulation of the host keyring
Syscall trace: pivot_root() invoked from inside a container

data_components.name: File Modification
data_components.definition: Filesystem writes from inside a container that target host paths via a hostPath mount. Writes to /etc, /usr, /var/lib/kubelet, or to runtime sockets are the strongest signal.
relevant_events: Write to a path that resolves outside the container's chroot via a hostPath bind
Write to /var/run/docker.sock or /var/run/containerd/containerd.sock from a container
Write to /etc/cron.* or /var/lib/kubelet/pods/*/credentials from a container
Write to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent from inside a container (cgroup release_agent escape; Falco stable rule covers this exactly)
Write to /proc/sysrq-trigger from inside a container

detection_strategies.name: Container escape via bind mounts, privileged containers, and runtime-socket abuse
detection_strategies.summary: Correlate the pod spec (declared escape primitives) with runtime evidence (syscall transitions, file writes to host paths, exec against runtime sockets). A high-fidelity alert requires both: a privileged or hostPath-bound pod is the precondition; the syscall or socket-abuse event is the consummation.

detection_strategies.name: Bind-mount, privileged, or docker.sock-based escape
detection_strategies.summary: Container escape attempts via hostPath bind mounts, privileged containers, or interaction with the container runtime socket from inside a container.

detection_strategies.name: Linux container escape via syscalls
detection_strategies.summary: Direct syscall-level escape: unshare, keyctl, mount, pivot_root invoked from inside a container PID namespace.

vendor_detections.title: Pod admitted with escape-class primitives
vendor_detections.intent: Surface every pod admitted with at least one escape primitive in its spec: privileged mode, dangerous capability, host namespace sharing, or hostPath mount targeting a sensitive path.
vendor_detections.query:
// Wiz Threat Center / Kubernetes Audit Log query (Resource Graph style)
let sensitivePaths = dynamic(["/", "/etc", "/var/run/docker.sock",
                              "/var/run/containerd/containerd.sock",
                              "/var/lib/kubelet", "/etc/kubernetes", "/proc"]);
let dangerousCaps  = dynamic(["SYS_ADMIN", "SYS_PTRACE", "SYS_MODULE",
                              "NET_ADMIN", "SYS_BOOT", "DAC_READ_SEARCH"]);
KubernetesAuditLog
| where verb == "create"
  and objectRef.resource == "pods"
  and stage == "ResponseComplete"
| extend pod  = requestObject
| extend privileged = tobool(pod.spec.containers[0].securityContext.privileged)
| extend caps_added = tostring(pod.spec.containers[0].securityContext.capabilities.add)
| extend hostPath_paths =
    tostring(extract_all(@"\"path\":\s*\"([^\"]+)\"", tostring(pod.spec.volumes)))
| where privileged == true
     or hostPath_paths has_any (sensitivePaths)
     or caps_added has_any (dangerousCaps)
     or tobool(pod.spec.hostPID) == true
     or tobool(pod.spec.hostNetwork) == true
     or tobool(pod.spec.hostIPC) == true
| project requestReceivedTimestamp,
          principal = user.username,
          namespace = objectRef.namespace,
          pod_name  = objectRef.name,
          privileged, caps_added, hostPath_paths
required_telemetry: Audit policy at RequestResponse level on pods so requestObject is captured
Constants for sensitivePaths and dangerousCaps maintained as enums, not inlined per-query
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: CNI/CSI/node-exporter DaemonSets legitimately need many of these primitives. Maintain an exception list keyed by service account, not by image.
vendor_detections.limitations: Pre-runtime only: this catches the declaration of the primitive, not the actual escape. Pair with the Falco rule below.

vendor_detections.title: Falco: container escape syscall trace
vendor_detections.intent: Detect runtime evidence of an escape attempt from inside a container: namespace-transition syscalls, exec of escape utilities, or writes to runtime sockets.
vendor_detections.query:
- list: container_escape_binaries
  items: [nsenter, unshare, chroot, runc, crictl, ctr, docker, kubectl, debugfs, mount]

- list: runtime_sockets
  items: [/var/run/docker.sock, /var/run/containerd/containerd.sock, /run/crio/crio.sock]

- macro: in_container
  condition: container.id != host

- rule: Container Escape Utility Executed
  desc: A known escape utility was executed inside a container.
  condition: spawned_process and in_container and proc.name in (container_escape_binaries)
  output: >
    Container escape utility executed
    (proc=%proc.name cmdline=%proc.cmdline pid_ns=%proc.pid_ns container=%container.name
     image=%container.image.repository user=%user.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [container, mitre_privilege_escalation, T1611]

- rule: Write To Runtime Socket From Container
  desc: Write to a container runtime socket from inside a container, indicating runtime takeover.
  condition: open_write and in_container and fd.name in (runtime_sockets)
  output: >
    Container wrote to runtime socket
    (fd=%fd.name proc=%proc.name container=%container.name image=%container.image.repository)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [container, mitre_privilege_escalation, T1611]
required_telemetry: Sysdig agent (or open-source Falco) deployed as a DaemonSet on every node
Modern syscall driver (eBPF-CO-RE) loaded so namespace fields are populated
container_escape_binaries and runtime_sockets lists kept in version control
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Service mesh sidecars and node-problem-detector occasionally exec nsenter against their own namespaces; allowlist by image+command, not by name alone.
vendor_detections.limitations: Direct syscalls (unshare, setns, mount) bypass the binary-name rule. Add a syscall-shape rule that targets the syscall directly when feasible (eBPF profiles).

vendor_detections.title: Upwind Explorer: namespace transition or write to host-bound mount
vendor_detections.intent: Capture in-kernel evidence of namespace traversal or host-mount writes, the two consummating signals of an actual escape rather than just a permissive pod spec. Authored as a Rego policy for Upwind Explorer, the documented custom-detection path.
required_telemetry: Upwind sensor (eBPF DaemonSet) on every node
Namespace and host-mount enrichment enabled so input.file.host_mount and input.process.namespaces.* are populated
Kubernetes correlation enabled to attribute input.container.id back to a workload
Upwind Explorer custom-policy authoring access for the tenant
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Some CNI plugins legitimately call setns to set up pod networking; suppress by pod label or DaemonSet identity rather than by syscall name.
vendor_detections.limitations: Requires a kernel new enough for the eBPF probe set; older nodes (RHEL 7-class) cannot supply this telemetry, fall back to the Falco rule there. The Upwind Explorer schema referenced above follows public docs/blog patterns and may need adjustment against the actual tenant schema.

mitre_cross_references.name: Deploy Container
mitre_cross_references.rationale: The writable hostPath mount is established at container creation time (T1610). MITRE T1611 page cites 'containers configured to mount the host's filesystem using the bind parameter' as the mechanism, and the Sigma rule 'kubernetes_audit_hostpath_mount' fires on T1611 at the pod creation (T1610) event -- the Sigma rule is tagged T1611 even though it fires on a T1610 (create pod) API call, because the mount is the precondition for the escape.

mitre_cross_references.name: Create or Modify System Process
mitre_cross_references.rationale: A writable hostPath mount exposes the host filesystem. MITRE T1611 Atomic Red Team test 2 ('Mount host filesystem to escape privileged Docker container') documents that after the escape the adversary drops cron jobs and payloads onto the host filesystem -- the host-filesystem write maps to T1543 (persistence via system process) or T1053 (scheduled task). The escape alone (T1611) is incomplete without the persistence step the mount enables.

mitre_cross_references.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After gaining a shell inside a container via kubectl exec (T1609), an adversary may write NOPASSWD: ALL to /etc/sudoers or a /etc/sudoers.d/ file to escalate from a non-root container user to root within the container. Observable: write to /etc/sudoers or exec of visudo inside the container PID namespace.

mitre_cross_references.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary can run chmod u+s on a binary to create a setuid persistence mechanism for future privilege escalation within the container. Applicable unless allowPrivilegeEscalation: false is set in the pod security context.

mitre_cross_references.name: Account Manipulation: SSH Authorized Keys
mitre_cross_references.rationale: From a shell obtained via kubectl exec into a container running sshd or a container with SSH access, an adversary appends their public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys to maintain persistent SSH access without valid credentials. Observable: write event to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Create Account: Local Account
mitre_cross_references.rationale: From a root shell in the container, an adversary runs useradd to create a backdoor account. MITRE explicitly lists Containers as a platform for this sub-technique. Observable: exec of /usr/sbin/useradd or write to /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Event Triggered Execution: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary modifies ~/.bashrc or /etc/profile to inject a payload that re-executes every time a shell session opens inside the container, including future kubectl exec sessions by operators. Observable: write to ~/.bashrc or /etc/profile inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Cron
mitre_cross_references.rationale: In containers that include crond (common in many base images), an adversary installs a crontab entry to re-execute a payload periodically after the initial kubectl exec session ends. Kinsing malware is documented using cron to download and re-run scripts every minute in container environments. Observable: write to /var/spool/cron/crontabs/ or exec of crontab -e inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container running a web server, an adversary drops a web shell into the web root directory, creating a persistent command execution channel via the already-exposed service port. Observable: write of a .php, .jsp, or .py file to a web-served directory inside the container, followed by an HTTP request to that path.

mitre_cross_references.name: Hijack Execution Flow: Dynamic Linker Hijacking
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary writes a malicious shared library and adds its path to /etc/ld.so.preload or sets LD_PRELOAD in the container environment to intercept application library calls. Hildegard malware, which specifically targets Kubernetes, is documented modifying /etc/ld.so.preload in container environments. Observable: write to /etc/ld.so.preload inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Process Injection: Ptrace System Calls
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container running as root or with CAP_SYS_PTRACE, an adversary uses ptrace to attach to the application process and extract credentials from memory or inject shellcode. Observable: ptrace syscall with PTRACE_ATTACH against a non-child process inside the container PID namespace.

mitre_cross_references.name: OS Credential Dumping: Proc Filesystem
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container as root, an adversary reads /proc/<pid>/maps and /proc/<pid>/mem to extract credentials from the application process memory (e.g., database passwords held in heap). LaZagne and MimiPenguin implement this technique. Observable: open/read syscall on /proc/<pid>/mem for a PID not owned by the calling process.

mitre_cross_references.name: OS Credential Dumping: /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container as root, an adversary reads /etc/shadow to dump password hashes for all local accounts for offline cracking. Observable: read of /etc/shadow by a process other than PAM or login utilities inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary searches for credentials in environment variables, config files, and mounted secrets including the Kubernetes service account token at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. MITRE explicitly lists Containers as a platform; Hildegard and TeamTNT are documented searching for these paths. Observable: read of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token or /run/secrets/* inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Unsecured Credentials: Shell History
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container that has been used interactively by operators, ~/.bash_history may contain plaintext credentials previously typed. Kinsing malware is documented searching bash_history files for credentials. Observable: read of ~/.bash_history by a process that is not the user's own shell.

mitre_cross_references.name: Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container used in CI/CD or mounting secret volumes, an adversary searches for SSH private keys and TLS certificates. Observable: find/read syscall on files matching *.pem, *.key, id_rsa patterns inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Command History
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After completing activity via kubectl exec, an adversary runs history -c or unset HISTFILE to erase evidence of their commands from the container. TeamTNT and Hildegard, both container-targeting malware families, are documented using this technique. Observable: exec of history -c inside a container terminal session.

mitre_cross_references.name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After dropping and executing a tool inside the container, an adversary runs rm -f on the tool binary to remove forensic artifacts. Observable: exec of rm targeting a recently-written executable inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: System Information Discovery
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary runs uname -a, cat /proc/version, and cat /etc/os-release to identify the kernel version and container OS to inform exploit selection. Observable: exec of uname, id, hostname, or cat /proc/version inside the container in rapid succession after initial access.

mitre_cross_references.name: Account Discovery: Local Account
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary reads /etc/passwd to enumerate user accounts and identify service accounts with home directories or elevated privileges. Observable: read of /etc/passwd by a process other than PAM inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Permission Groups Discovery: Local Groups
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary runs groups or reads /etc/group to identify membership in privileged groups such as sudo, docker, or adm. Observable: exec of groups or id inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Process Discovery
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary runs ps aux or reads /proc/*/cmdline to enumerate running processes, identify applications holding credentials in memory, and (if hostPID=true) discover all host processes. Observable: exec of ps or pgrep inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: File and Directory Discovery
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary uses find / or ls -la to enumerate the filesystem for configuration files, secrets, and mounted volumes. Observable: exec of find / or recursive directory traversal targeting /var/run/secrets/, /etc/, or mounted volume paths.

mitre_cross_references.name: Network Service Discovery
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary uses nmap or nc -z to scan the pod network for reachable services including the Kubernetes API server at kubernetes.default.svc, etcd, and adjacent pod services. MITRE explicitly lists Containers as a platform. Observable: exec of nmap or nc -z inside the container; DNS query for kubernetes.default.svc.

mitre_cross_references.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary reads ip addr, ip route, and /etc/resolv.conf to learn the pod CIDR, gateway, and DNS server (kube-dns) to inform lateral movement. Observable: exec of ip addr or cat /etc/resolv.conf inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary uses curl or wget to download exploit binaries, cryptominers, or lateral movement tools from an external C2. Hildegard and Doki malware are documented using tool download into containers. Observable: outbound HTTP/HTTPS from the container to an external IP not in the application's documented egress list.

mitre_cross_references.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container that includes Python (common in data and ML workloads), an adversary executes python3 one-liners for reverse shells, enumeration, or payload delivery. Observable: exec of python3 -c with socket/subprocess imports inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Resource Hijacking: Compute Hijacking
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary drops and runs a cryptominer (e.g., xmrig) to abuse the pod's CPU allocation. MITRE explicitly lists Containers as a platform; TeamTNT, Hildegard, and Kinsing are documented executing cryptominers inside containers via this exact path. Observable: exec of xmrig or similar binary inside the container; sustained high CPU from a non-application process.

mitre_cross_references.name: Data Destruction
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container with mounted persistent volumes, an adversary runs rm -rf targeting volume mount paths to destroy application data. MITRE explicitly lists Containers as a platform; the technique page's detection strategy specifically mentions rm -rf /mnt/volumes/ inside containers. Observable: exec of rm -rf targeting a mounted volume path inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: File and Directory Permissions Modification: Linux and Mac File Permissions
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary uses chmod or chown to make a dropped payload executable or to restrict operator access to their persistence files. Kinsing, which targets containers, is documented using chmod on key files. Observable: exec of chmod +x or chown on a recently-written file inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container, an adversary places their tool binary in /tmp/ or /dev/shm/ with a name matching a legitimate system utility (e.g., kube-apiserver, sshd) to evade process-name-based detection. MITRE explicitly lists Containers as a platform and the technique page includes container-specific language. Observable: exec of a binary in /tmp/ or /dev/shm/ whose name matches a known system tool.

mitre_cross_references.name: Remote Services: SSH
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container and obtaining SSH keys or credentials, an adversary uses the container as a pivot point to SSH to other pods or cluster nodes. Kinsing malware is documented using SSH for lateral movement from container environments. Observable: outbound TCP to port 22 from inside the container to a pod or node IP.

mitre_cross_references.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container as a non-root user, an adversary executes a local privilege escalation exploit (e.g., CVE-2022-0847 DirtyPipe, CVE-2021-4034 pkexec) to become root within the container or to break out to the host. MITRE lists Containers as a platform and analytic AN1422 explicitly covers container breakout via exploitation. Observable: exec of a known exploit binary or anomalous write to /proc/self/mem inside the container.

mitre_cross_references.name: Compromise Host Software Binary
mitre_cross_references.rationale: After exec into a container as root, an adversary replaces a common binary (/usr/bin/ssh, /bin/ls) with a trojanized version that backdoors authentication or hides files within the container's writable filesystem layer. Observable: write to /usr/bin/, /usr/sbin/, or /bin/ inside the container for a file already present; file checksum mismatch vs. original image layer.

mitre_cross_references.name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Compile After Delivery
mitre_cross_references.rationale: In containers that include a build toolchain (gcc, go, make), an adversary transfers source code and compiles it inside the container to avoid dropping a binary that would match known malware hashes. Observable: exec of gcc, go build, or make in /tmp/ inside a container at an unexpected time; resulting binary exec immediately after compilation.
